steps.text: An **opening** is the first stretch of a game, roughly the first ten moves. Your pieces start boxed in behind the pawns, so most of them cannot move at all. The opening has one job: get your pieces out and your king safe before the fighting starts. The next board shows what is stuck at the start, and which single move frees two pieces.

steps.title: Centre pawn, edge pawn
steps.prompt: In the second case White opened with the edge pawn a4 instead of e4. Predict first: can the bishop on f1 move?

steps.caption: Of the pieces, only the knights can move at the start. The bishops, queen and king are boxed in by their own pawns.

line.say: One pawn move opens a diagonal for the bishop on f1 and another for the queen on d1.
Black does the same on its side of the board.

steps.caption: After the centre pawn moves, the bishop on f1 reaches five squares and the queen on d1 reaches four.

line.say: The bishop jumps out to a long open diagonal and now looks toward Black's side.
